title: The Morning Brief: Van Bommel takes Belgium helm; Romo arrested; heat runs through sports
dek: Belgium hired Mark van Bommel as head coach on a Euro 2028 contract, replacing Rudi Garcia. In separate news, CBS analyst Tony Romo was arrested on suspicion of OWI in Milwaukee with a September court date. Six other stories span doping bans, roster extensions, broadcast disputes, and injury setbacks across soccer, cycling, NFL, golf, and boxing.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Van Bommel's appointment signals Belgium's reset after a World Cup quarterfinal exit, while Romo's arrest creates uncertainty around his CBS role pending adjudication. Meanwhile, operational clarifications (the NFL's 17-game schedule through 2027, the Duke-Texas Tech basketball swap) and athletic setbacks (Sonnett's knee, Langton's fall, Schrager's doping ban) reshape multiple sports' near-term planning.
bottom_line: Belgium's managerial reset, Romo's arrest, and broadcast clarity in college basketball mark the morning's clearest beats; beneath them run several layers of injury and disciplinary limbo (Sonnett's knee, Schrager's doping case, Langton's fall, the Senegal appeal heading to October). What emerges from Sonnett's medical evaluation in New Jersey, when Romo's court date arrives in September, and whether Schrager appeals the NADP decision will determine the scope of consequences across multiple sports. Watch for CBS's statement on Romo's on-air status, any follow-up detail on Langton's condition, and the secondary analysis on Volpato's oral fluid sample.
body: Belgium named Mark van Bommel, 49, as head coach on a contract through Euro 2028, effective August 15, replacing Rudi Garcia whose tenure ended after a World Cup quarterfinal loss to Spain. Van Bommel, a former Netherlands captain with experience at Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and AC Milan as a player, arrives from Royal Antwerp, where he won the Belgian league title in 2023, the club's first since 1957. His appointment reflects the federation's intent to build on recent tournament progress with a manager whose domestic record proves tactical competence.

Off the field, CBS's lead NFL analyst Tony Romo was arrested in Milwaukee on Thursday on suspicion of operating a vehicle while under the influence. Romo, 46, was stopped while driving south on Interstate 43 and performed poorly on field sobriety tests, per the Milwaukee County Sheriff's Office arrest report. He has a court appearance scheduled for September 21. Neither his legal outcome nor CBS's response to his on-air role is determined; the network has made no statement on his status pending adjudication.

In college basketball, Duke and Michigan's December 21 nonconference game at Madison Square Garden, originally hampered by broadcast-rights disputes tied to Duke's exclusive Amazon Prime Video deal, has been canceled entirely. Texas Tech will replace Michigan in the same time slot at MSG on Prime Video. The sources do not identify which party bears responsibility for the broadcast-rights misinterpretation, leaving the specific contractual failure unresolved.

The NFL confirmed Super Bowl LXII for February 13, 2028, in Atlanta, effectively locking the 2027 season into a 17-game schedule and pushing any 18-game expansion to at least 2028. The date removes operational uncertainty for Atlanta and broadcasters but leaves the labor question, the players union opposes the expansion while owners favor it, unresolved heading into formal bargaining.

In professional sports, the Boston Celtics extended forward Jordan Walsh for three years and $15 million through 2029-30, locking in a below-market rate for a young wing who shot 38 percent from three-point range this season. Separately, Stephen Fulton Jr., a two-division world champion, missed weight by 6.5 pounds for his bout against Liam Wilson in Sydney, canceling the fight. This marks Fulton's second consecutive weight miss, raising questions about whether regulatory bodies will impose consequences for repeated failures.

In combat sports, Tyson Fury stopped Mariusz Wach by seventh-round stoppage in Pattaya, Thailand, clearing the path to a November heavyweight unification fight with Anthony Joshua. Fury improved to 36-2-1 with 25 knockouts; his bout with Joshua is contingent on Joshua's Saturday performance against Prenga and both camps' adherence to the November timeline.

In cycling and track, Tadej Pogacar won stage 19 of the Tour de France at Alpe d'Huez, launching a solo attack from more than three minutes down with 12 kilometers remaining. His victory extends his overall lead to 7 minutes 11 seconds over Remco Evenepoel with two stages left. Separately, Noah Lyles won the 100m at the U.S. athletics championships with a time of 9.79 seconds, the world-leading time for 2026.

In golf, Michael Kim shot a 12-under 59 on Friday at the 3M Open in Blaine, Minnesota, becoming only the 15th golfer in PGA Tour history to break 60. The bogey-free round included four consecutive birdies to close and gave Kim a three-shot lead heading into the weekend with a tournament total of 14-under.

Several athletes face injury and disciplinary uncertainty. Emily Sonnett, a starting center back for Gotham FC and 118-cap USWNT veteran, was stretchered off in the 7th minute of Friday's 2-2 draw with Portland Thorns after suffering a non-contact left knee injury; her diagnosis and timeline remain unknown pending evaluation in New Jersey. Daphne Schrager, a Paris 2024 Paralympic silver medalist in cycling, has been handed a two-year ban following a positive test for Ligandrol; the ban is backdated to June 2, 2025 and expires June 1, 2027, leaving her eligible for the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics but ineligible for the current Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Gabriel Langton, an 18-year-old English gymnast, fell off the high bar during the men's team final at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and was stretchered off with a serious head and neck injury; his condition and full extent of injuries remain unreported.

In African football, the Confederation of African Football's decision to strip Senegal of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, awarding it instead to Morocco on disciplinary grounds after Senegal left the pitch in protest of a penalty award, faces its first full hearing at the Court of Arbitration for Sport on October 8. Senegal won the final 1-0 on the pitch on January 18. Separately, the Women's Africa Cup of Nations begins July 26 in Morocco and runs through August 16, featuring 16 teams divided into four groups; defending champion Nigeria and hosts Morocco are among the contenders.

In Australian soccer, Cristian Volpato, a 22-year-old midfielder who appeared in the World Cup in July 2026, allegedly tested positive for cocaine during a roadside drug test after being stopped for speeding on Sydney's Anzac Bridge at 1:10 AM on Friday. A secondary oral fluid sample was taken for further analysis. In ice hockey, Vegas did not retain interim coach John Tortorella following the Stanley Cup Final loss to the Hurricanes, opting instead to promote AHL coach Ryan Craig as originally planned. Tortorella led Vegas from eight games down in the regular season through the playoffs, sweeping Colorado in the Western Conference Finals before losing the championship in six games.
